description: Backend plumbing for stateless reveal tokens and in-memory wish lists. Adds two config properties (token.secret, app.base-url), extends AmigoProperties with two nested static classes, and creates two new Spring services. No changes to existing web endpoints or email sending logic — FEAT-002 builds on top of this. Independent of FEAT-002.
steps:
Step 1 — Edit src/main/resources/application.yml: under the existing `amigo:` block (after the `mail:` sub-block) add: `  token:
    secret: ${TOKEN_SECRET:amigo-invisible-secret-key-padding}
  app:
    base-url: ${APP_BASE_URL:http://localhost:8080}`. Preserve all existing indentation and content.

Step 2 — Edit src/main/java/com/dgc/amigoinvisible/config/AmigoProperties.java: (a) add two new fields to the class body: `private Token token = new Token();` and `private App app = new App();`. (b) Add two new nested static inner classes after the existing Mail class, both annotated with @Getter and @Setter: `public static class Token { private String secret = "amigo-invisible-secret-key-padding"; }` and `public static class App { private String baseUrl = "http://localhost:8080"; }`. Follow the exact same pattern as the existing Participants/Exclusions/Mail classes.

Step 3 — Create src/main/java/com/dgc/amigoinvisible/service/TokenService.java: @Slf4j @Service with a manually written constructor (NOT @RequiredArgsConstructor, because initialization logic is needed). Constructor takes AmigoProperties, derives a 16-byte AES key by MD5-hashing the secret, and stores it as a final SecretKeySpec field. Method `createToken(String senderName, String senderEmail, String receiverName, String receiverEmail, String drawId)`: builds payload `drawId|senderName|senderEmail|receiverName|receiverEmail`, generates 16-byte random IV via SecureRandom, encrypts with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding (javax.crypto.Cipher), prepends IV to ciphertext, returns Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(combined). Method `decode(String token)`: Base64URL-decodes, splits IV (first 16 bytes) from ciphertext, decrypts, splits payload on '|' with limit 5, returns Optional<AssignmentData> or Optional.empty() on any exception. Inner public record: `AssignmentData(String drawId, String senderName, String senderEmail, String receiverName, String receiverEmail)`. Imports: javax.crypto.Cipher, javax.crypto.spec.IvParameterSpec, javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec, java.security.MessageDigest, java.security.SecureRandom, java.util.Arrays, java.util.Base64, java.util.Optional, java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.

Step 4 — Create src/main/java/com/dgc/amigoinvisible/service/WishListService.java: @Service (no Lombok constructor annotation needed — no injected dependencies). Field: `private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, String> wishes = new ConcurrentHashMap<>()`. Method `save(String email, String text)`: calls `wishes.put(normalise(email), text)`. Method `get(String email)`: returns `Optional.ofNullable(wishes.get(normalise(email)))`. Private static helper `normalise(String email)`: returns `email.toLowerCase().trim()`, handling null by returning empty string.
acceptance_criteria: application.yml has `amigo.token.secret` and `amigo.app.base-url` entries that can be overridden by TOKEN_SECRET and APP_BASE_URL env vars respectively.
AmigoProperties.getToken().getSecret() and AmigoProperties.getApp().getBaseUrl() are accessible after Spring context starts.
TokenService.createToken(...) returns a non-null Base64URL string with no '=' padding.
TokenService.decode(token) called with the result of createToken(...) returns Optional containing the original AssignmentData with all five fields intact.
WishListService.save(email, text) followed by WishListService.get(email) returns Optional.of(text).
WishListService.get(email) for an unsaved email returns Optional.empty().
WishListService normalises email case: save('A@B.COM', 'x') then get('a@b.com') returns Optional.of('x').
verification: Run `mvn compile` from c:\projects\DGC\amigo-invisible — must exit 0 with BUILD SUCCESS.
Run `mvn test` from c:\projects\DGC\amigo-invisible — must exit 0 (no test failures; no test classes exist so this mainly verifies Spring context loads).
findings: AmigoProperties Token/App nested classes use @Getter/@Setter on the static inner class, same as Mail. TokenService uses a manual constructor (not @RequiredArgsConstructor) because key derivation runs at init time. WishListService has no injected deps so no constructor annotation is needed. FEAT-002 needs: (a) inject TokenService + AmigoProperties into EmailService (manual constructor — add parameter, assign field); (b) generate token and revealLink inside sendAssignmentEmails using a.sender().name(), a.sender().email(), a.receiver().name(), a.receiver().email(), drawId; (c) create RevealController.java with GET /reveal/{token} and POST /reveal/{token}/wishes; (d) create reveal.html Thymeleaf template.
